title: Lesson 2: Relating the Standard & Vertex Forms: Completing the Square
goal: Rewrite standard form into vertex form by completing the square, so the high or low point is readable.
you_will_need: Paper, tiles or a sketched square, and the graph board on this page.
credits: Ontario curriculum sample: Queen’s Printer for Ontario
Water arc photo: GuidoB, CC BY-SA 3.0

blocks.alt: Two streams of water shoot from nozzles on a stone fountain rim and fall back into the basin. Each stream makes a smooth downward-opening arc; the highest point of each arc is visible against a park fence and trees.

blocks.text: You need the highest point. This time you only have the expanded writing.

blocks.prompt: Do not sketch a careful graph yet. What about this writing makes the peak hard to name?

blocks.text: Standard form makes the \(y\)-intercept easy to see. Vertex form makes the turning point easy to see.

blocks.prompt: You are handed only standard form. Which writing would make the vertex readable?

stages.worked: Reverse last lesson’s expand, then see the square and match the algebra.
stages.practise: A new a = 1 case, factor a first, then a simple fraction, then check the graph.
stages.extend: Sketch key features. Try another for a sketch-plan choice.

blocks.text: Same curve, both ways
Expand, then complete the square. Same graph?

blocks.prompt: Do the two writings sit on one curve?

blocks.text: See the square first
Name the side and the leftover. Algebra comes next.

blocks.prompt: What in the picture is the side? What is the leftover?

blocks.text: Match the algebra
Write vertex form for the same function.

blocks.prompt: How does the writing match the side and the leftover?

blocks.text: Your turn
Same steps. New numbers.

blocks.prompt: How do you read h from the brackets?

blocks.text: When a is not 1
Factor a from the x terms first.

blocks.prompt: If a stayed 1, what inside the brackets would go wrong?

blocks.text: A simple fraction
Same steps. Half of 1/2 is a fraction.

blocks.prompt: Which step matched the integer cases?

blocks.text: Check the graph
Complete the square, then overlay.

blocks.prompt: Do both writings give the same outputs?

blocks.text: Sketch key features
Vertex, axis, max or min. Not a list of intervals.

blocks.prompt: How did completing the square make the vertex readable?

blocks.text: Try another: which sketch plan?
Choose factoring or completing the square. One reason each. No formula.

blocks.prompt: What feature made each choice a fit?

blocks.text: On paper: expand and complete the square on the shared model, then check a few table points on one sketch.
Completing the square rewrites \(ax^2 + bx + c\) as \(a(x - h)^2 + k\). The graph does not move.

items: See the square and leftover before the algebra when you can.
When a is not 1, factor a from the x^2 and x terms first.
A simple rational b/a uses the same steps.
Plus inside the brackets still means h is negative.

blocks.text: Back to the stream. You still have only the expanded writing.
Do not move the board yet.

blocks.prompt: How did completing the square name the high point?
